title: Data Pipeline (ETL)
description: Build an ETL pipeline framework with extractors, transformers, loaders, error handling, and pipeline composition.

steps.title: Create data source extractors
steps.description: Build extractor functions that read data from different sources. Implement `arrayExtractor(data)` that returns the array as-is, `generatorExtractor(gen)` that exhausts a generator and returns all items, and `simulatedFileExtractor(filePath)` that reads a simulated file (an array of lines). Each extractor should return an object with `{ data, source, recordCount }`. Print the extracted data and record count.
hints: arrayExtractor: just wrap data with metadata: { data: arr, source: 'array', recordCount: arr.length }
generatorExtractor: use a for...of loop or list() to consume the generator
simulatedFileExtractor: accept an array of strings as 'file lines' and parse them (e.g. CSV-like splitting)

verification.successMessage: All three extractors produce data with correct metadata!
verification.failureMessage: Print the extracted data and recordCount for each extractor type (array, generator, file).

steps.title: Implement data transformers
steps.description: Create transformer functions that can be chained together. Implement `filterTransform(predicate)` that filters records, `mapTransform(fn)` that transforms each record, and `aggregateTransform(key, fn)` that groups records by a key and applies an aggregation function. Chain these together: extract numbers, filter evens, map to strings, then aggregate by parity. Print the output of each step.
hints: Each transform returns a function that takes data and returns transformed data
Chain by passing the output of one transform as input to the next
aggregateTransform should use a Map or dict to group by key, then apply fn to each group

verification.successMessage: Transformers chain together correctly with filter, map, and aggregate!
verification.failureMessage: Print the output after each transformation step in the chain.

steps.title: Build data sink loaders
steps.description: Implement loader functions that consume transformed data. Create `consoleLoader()` that prints each record, `arrayLoader()` that collects records into an internal array (accessible via `.getData()`), and `accumulatorLoader(reduceFn, initial)` that reduces records into a single value. Load the transformed output from step 2 into all three loaders and print the results.
hints: consoleLoader: return { load: (records) => records.forEach(r => console.log('Record:', r)) }
arrayLoader: store records in an internal array, expose getData() to retrieve them
accumulatorLoader: call reduceFn on each record, maintaining an accumulator starting from initial

verification.successMessage: All three loaders consume data and produce correct output!
verification.failureMessage: Print each record through consoleLoader and show the accumulated result.

steps.title: Add error handling with retry
steps.description: Wrap pipeline steps with error handling. Implement a `withRetry(step, options)` wrapper that retries a step up to `maxRetries` times with exponential backoff if it throws. Also implement `withErrorFallback(step, fallbackFn)` that catches errors and calls a fallback function. Test by creating a transformer that fails on certain inputs and show retry attempts and fallback results.
hints: withRetry: try the step, catch error, wait backoffMs * 2^attempt, retry up to maxRetries
withErrorFallback: try the step, on error call fallbackFn(error) and return its result
Print 'Retry attempt X of Y' during retries so the user can see the retry logic

verification.successMessage: Error handling correctly retries failed steps and uses fallbacks!
verification.failureMessage: Print retry attempt numbers and show that the fallback result is used after max retries.

steps.title: Implement pipeline composition
steps.description: Build a `Pipeline` class that chains extract -> transform -> load. Constructor takes an extractor, an array of transformers, and a loader. Implement a `run()` method that executes the full pipeline and returns the final result. Support `.pipe()` for method chaining. Build a pipeline that extracts numbers, filters > 5, maps to strings, and loads to array. Print the final output.
hints: run() should call extract(), then apply each transform in sequence, then call loader.load()
.pipe() returns 'this' (the Pipeline instance) to enable chaining
Include a stage tracking array that logs which stage is executing

verification.successMessage: Pipeline correctly composes extract, transform, and load stages in sequence!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Pipeline running: <stage>' for each stage as the pipeline executes.

steps.title: Add pipeline metrics
steps.description: Instrument the pipeline with performance metrics. Track execution time per stage (using high-resolution timers), record counts entering and leaving each stage, and error counts. Implement `getMetrics()` that returns a formatted report. Run a pipeline over 1000 records and print the full metrics report showing stage names, durations, record counts, and error stats.
hints: Use process.hrtime(), performance.now(), or time.perf_counter() for timing
Before and after each stage, record: stageName, inputCount, outputCount, durationMs, errors
getMetrics() should print a formatted table or multi-line report

verification.successMessage: Pipeline metrics report shows timing, record counts, and error stats per stage!
verification.failureMessage: Print a metrics report with each stage's name, duration in ms, input/output record counts, and any errors.
